panel.summary: Unit spec never asserts the new `types: { getTypeParser: datasourceTypeParser }` client option or the RAW_TEXT_OIDS parser logic
panel.evidence: datasource.service.spec.ts was updated only to add the two new `SET` statements (nth-calls 2 and 3). The mocked `Client` constructor args are not asserted for the new `types` option, and `datasourceTypeParser`/`RAW_TEXT_OIDS` (the actual behavioural core of this change — DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ returned as raw text, everything else delegated to the default parser) has no unit test at all. It is only covered indirectly by the DATABASE_URL-gated e2e test, so if that lane is skipped the parser change ships with no coverage. A direct unit assertion (parser for TIMESTAMP returns input verbatim, parser for INT4 still parses to number) would be cheap.
panel.finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::unit spec never asserts the new `types: { gettypeparser: datasourcetypeparser }` client option or the raw_text_oids parser logic

coderabbit.summary: Avoid using `SET DateStyle` to normalize output
coderabbit.detail: **Avoid using `SET DateStyle` to normalize output** This session setting alters input parsing semantics, not just output formatting. Under `'ISO, MDY'`, ambiguous literals like `'01/02/2025'::date` are parsed as January 2nd within this session, overriding the database's default interpretation for these queries. This introduces inconsistent results for valid user queries sent via `executeQuery()`. Rely on the custom `getTypeParser` implementation for formatting control instead.

evidence: Panel: the unit spec never asserts the new `types: { getTypeParser }` option or the RAW_TEXT_OIDS logic — a coverage gap. CodeRabbit: `SET DateStyle` alters input parsing semantics — a behaviour objection. Adding the test does not remove the SET; removing the SET does not add the test.
